opex.text: Liquidity refers to our ability to generate sufficient cash to meet our financial obligations, which arise primarily from the withdrawal of deposits, extension of credit and payment of operating expenses. Liquidity risk is the risk that the Bank’s financial condition or overall safety and soundness is adversely affected by an inability (or perceived inability) to meet its obligations. Our ongoing philosophy is to remain in a liquid position, as reflected by such indicators as the composition of our earning assets, typically including some level of reverse repurchase agreements; federal funds sold; balances at the Federal Reserve Bank; and/or other short-term investments; asset quality; well-capitalized position; and profitable operating results. Our Asset Liability Management Committee (“ALCO”) is charged with the responsibility of monitoring policies designed to ensure acceptable composition of our asset/liability mix. We have employed our funds in a manner to provide liquidity from both assets and liabilities sufficient to meet our cash needs. The Company also continues to monitor liquidity conditions and maintains a contingency funding plan and performs specific procedures, including scenario analyses and stress testing, to evaluate and maintain appropriate levels of available liquidity in alignment with liquidity risk.

prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL)
prov.text: SouthState utilizes economic forecasts provided by a third-party service provider and applies probability weightings to multiple economic scenarios based on management's assessment of economic and market conditions. As a sensitivity analysis, applying a 100% weighting to the adverse scenario would increase the ACL by approximately $207 million, while applying a 100% weighting to the upside scenario would decrease the ACL by approximately $145 million. The adverse scenario reflects recessionary economic conditions, while the upside scenario reflects stronger-than-expected economic performance. This analysis is hypothetical and does not represent management's estimate of expected credit losses as of September 30, 2026.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Noninterest expense increased by $2.4 million, or 0.7%, in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, primarily resulted from the following expenses:

Salaries and employee benefits increased primarily due to higher commission and incentive expense of $9.8 million, as well as an increase in salary expense of $7.9 million, resulting primarily from merit increases and an increase in the number of employees due to growth in sales force.

Occupancy expense increased in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025, due mainly to increases in lease expenses and building occupancy expense, including related depreciation, of $1.3 million and $1.0 million, respectively.

OREO expense and loan related expense decreased primarily due to a $2.6 million decrease in losses on sales of OREO.

Amortization of intangibles decreased by $2.8 million, or 11.9%, due to lower amortization expense related to the core deposit intangible recognized in connection with the Independent acquisition, which is subject to accelerated amortization in the earlier periods of its estimated life.

Business development and staff related expense increased due mainly to higher employee travel and entertainment, and recruitment-related costs of approximately $1.5 million.

FDIC assessment and other regulatory charges increased primarily due to an increase in the FDIC assessment rat.

tax.text: Our effective tax rate was 22.91% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 23.25% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the effective rate for the current quarter, when compared to the same period in the prior year, was driven primarily by lower non-deductible executive compensation during the current quarter, as well as non-deductible merger expenses recognized in the third quarter of 2025 related to the acquisition of Independent completed on January 1, 2025. In addition, there was an increase in tax-exempt interest income in the current quarter compared to the same period in 2025. This was partially offset by a decrease in the cash surrender value of BOLI policies in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the third quarter of 2025.

net.text: We reported consolidated net income of $223.8 million, or diluted earnings per share (“EPS”) of $2.30, for the third quarter of 2026 compared to consolidated net income of $246.6 million, or diluted EPS of $2.42, in the comparable period of 2025, a 9.3% decrease in consolidated net income and a 5.0% decrease in diluted EPS. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we reported consolidated net income of $679.6 million, or diluted EPS of $6.93, compared to consolidated net income of $550.9 million, or diluted EPS of $5.41, in the comparable period of 2025, a 23.4% increase in consolidated net income and a 28.1% increase in diluted EPS. Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income and Margin
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income is the Company’s principal source of income and a key driver of overall financial performance. Net interest income and net interest margin are affected by the level and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, as well as changes in long-term and short-term market interest rates. On September 16, 2026, the Federal Reserve increased the target federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a range to 3.75% to 4.00%, which remained in effect as of September 30, 2026. This followed reductions totaling 75 basis points in the second half of 2025. Despite the September 2026 increase in the federal funds target range, interest rate conditions during the third quarter of 2026 were lower compared to the third quarter of 2025, impacting both asset yields and funding costs.

The decline in non-tax equivalent and the Tax Equivalent (“TE”) net interest margin of 28 basis points in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter of 2025 primarily reflected lower yields on interest-earning assets, driven by reduced loan accretion income and a lower interest rate environment, partially offset by lower funding costs and balance-sheet mix changes.

Lower non-TE yield on interest-earning assets was primarily driven by lower loan yields, largely attributable to continued runoff of acquired loans and a reduction in loan accretion income of approximately…

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income provides us with additional revenues that are significant sources of income. For the three months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, noninterest income comprised 13.7%, and 14.2%, respectively, of total net interest income and noninterest income. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, and 2025, noninterest income comprised 14.4%, and 13.6%, respectively, of total net interest income and noninterest income.

Noninterest income decreased during the third quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. This quarterly change in total noninterest income resulted from the following:

Correspondent banking and capital markets income was lower, primarily attributable to a $4.0 million decrease in income generated from the sale of customer swap ARC hedges, reflecting decreased hedging activity as commercial borrowers showed less demand to convert variable-rate loans to fixed rates. The decrease was also driven by higher expense associated with variation margin payments for centrally cleared swaps where we recorded an expense of $5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to an expense of $4.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. In addition, other operational revenue was lower by approximately $2.4 million.

Noninterest income increased during the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

intro.text: SouthState Bank Corporation (“We,” “Our,” “SouthState” or the “Company”) is a financial holding company headquartered in Winter Haven, Florida. During the third quarter of 2025, the Company was redomiciled to the state of Florida by merging SouthState Corporation, a South Carolina corporation, with and into SouthState Bank Corporation, a Florida corporation that was wholly-owned by SouthState Corporation prior to such merger, and adopting its name. We provide a wide range of banking services and products to our customers through our wholly owned bank subsidiary, SouthState Bank, National Association (the “Bank”), a national banking association, from our headquarters branch in Winter Haven, Florida and, as of December 31, 2025, a 342-branch network located throughout Florida, South Carolina, Texas, Georgia, Colorado, North Carolina, Alabama, and Virginia.
